title: Fang Bo, the 2015 world finalist, signs for Fulda-Maberzell in the Tischtennis Bundesliga
seo_title: Fang Bo signs for Fulda-Maberzell in the Bundesliga
description: Fang Bo, 34, joins TTC Fulda-Maberzell for the second half of the Bundesliga season, replacing Andrei Istrate, two weeks after his Istanbul title.
standfirst: The former China international, now playing for Kazakhstan, has a contract to the end of the season and takes the place of Andrei Istrate, who is leaving at his own request.
body: Fang Bo, who reached the men's singles final at the 2015 World Championships, has signed for TTC RhönSprudel Fulda-Maberzell and will play in the Tischtennis Bundesliga from the second half of the season.

The 34-year-old has a contract until the end of the 2026-27 season. He takes the place of Andrei Istrate, the 21-year-old Romanian, who is leaving the club after half a season at his own request. The club announced the signing on Friday, a fortnight after Fang won [WTT Contender Istanbul](/news/wtt-contender-istanbul-2026-finals-fang-bo-honoka-hashimoto-titles.html) as a wild card ranked 160th.

Stefan Frauenholz, the Fulda-Maberzell president, pointed to that title. "With his win at WTT Contender Istanbul in November, he has shown impressively that he belongs among the top international players," he said (translated from German).

The club said Fang's attacking game and experience at the highest level would give the head coach, Qing Yu Meng, more options, and called the signing an important step in its sporting development. Fans in Fulda, it said, could look forward to a player who had already made his mark on the biggest international stage.

Fang's career peak came in Suzhou in 2015, when he beat Xu Xin and Zhang Jike on his way to the world final before losing to Ma Long. He was ranked as high as eighth in the world and won the 2016 World Team Championships with China. He left the national team in 2021 and returned to international play in April this year representing Kazakhstan, under terms that keep him out of the Olympics, the World Championships and the World Cup.
His Istanbul title was his first international singles title since 2013 and lifted him 94 places in the world ranking. He is now the world No 65.

Fang has not played on the WTT tour since. He [pulled out of WTT Star Contender Muscat](/news/fang-bo-withdraws-wtt-star-contender-muscat-2026-injury-treatment.html) during qualifying on 17 November, saying he had needed two injections to get through the injury and was going home for treatment. His coach in Istanbul, Li Liangfu, said Fang had played that event with a neck injury. Neither Fang nor the club has said when he expects to be fit, and the club's announcement did not mention it.

A move to Germany had been talked about for a week. Chinese social media reports said Fang told a livestream on 20 November that he would play in the Bundesliga to get more high-intensity matches, without naming a club.

Fulda-Maberzell are eighth of 12 with three wins from nine matches, six points behind TTF Ochsenhausen in fourth, the last play-off place. Five of their six defeats have been by 3-2, the last of them at home to TSV Bad Königshofen on 13 November, before a 3-0 win at ASC Grünwettersbach last weekend.

Dimitrij Ovtcharov, the world No 21, has carried them, winning eight of his 11 singles. Ruwen Filus has won four of six, Jonathan Groth three of seven and Fanbo Meng two of eight. Istrate, ranked 165th, played in only three matches, all in August: he lost his only singles, 3-0 to Benedikt Duda at Bergneustadt, and played in the deciding doubles in the other two.

Fulda-Maberzell finish the first half of the season at home to Borussia Düsseldorf, the unbeaten leaders, on 13 December and at 1. FC Saarbrücken on 18 December. The second half starts with home matches against Werder Bremen on 7 January and ASC Grünwettersbach on 9 January.

On 16 January Fulda go to Düsseldorf, whose squad includes Fang's former China teammate Fan Zhendong. Fan lost a Bundesliga singles for the first time this season to Eduard Ionescu last Sunday, [as Eleven reported](/news/tischtennis-bundesliga-2026-27-matchday-9-ionescu-beats-fan-zhendong-dusseldorf-win.html).
